introduction: CADMIZORB-PLUS soft-gel capsules combine calcium carbonate 200 mg with calcitriol 0.25 mcg, the active form of vitamin D, plus vitamin K2-7, methylcobalamin (vitamin B12), magnesium, boron and zinc. It is used to treat calcium deficiency and to support bone health, including in people with osteoporosis.

Take it at the same time each day, exactly as your doctor prescribes, and do not take more than advised. Because calcitriol is a strong form of vitamin D, your doctor may check your blood calcium during treatment. Tell your doctor about any other medicines and supplements you take, especially other vitamin D or calcium products.
uses: Supporting bone health in osteoporosis and low bone density

benefits.text: Calcium is needed for strong bones and teeth, and for normal nerve, muscle and heart function. Calcium carbonate tops up the calcium in your diet, and calcitriol, the active form of vitamin D, helps your gut absorb it. Magnesium and zinc also support normal bone metabolism.

In osteoporosis, bones become thinner and more likely to break. Calcium with active vitamin D helps maintain bone mineral density, while vitamin K2-7 activates proteins that help bind calcium into bone. Your doctor may prescribe it alongside other osteoporosis treatment.

sideEffects: High blood calcium with long-term or excessive use (see warnings)
clinical.howToUse: Take this medicine in the dose and for the length of time your doctor advises. Swallow the capsule whole with water; do not chew or break it. Taking it with or after a meal can help calcium absorption and reduce stomach upset.

Methylcobalamin is an active form of vitamin B12, needed for healthy nerves and red blood cells.

Avoid other vitamin D products, including high-dose vitamin D supplements, unless your doctor advises them.
The risk of high calcium is greater if you are immobile for long periods, for example after surgery.
If you are on long-term kidney dialysis, your doctor will decide whether this product is suitable, because it contains magnesium as well as calcitriol.
Tell your doctor if you have kidney disease, kidney stones or a heart rhythm problem.

Vitamin D toxicity
Calcium deposits in body tissues (metastatic calcification)
Allergy to any ingredient of the capsule
interactions: Thiazide water tablets, such as hydrochlorothiazide, can increase the risk of high calcium.
High calcium can increase the risk of heart rhythm problems in people taking digoxin.
Vitamin K2-7 can reduce the effect of blood thinners such as warfarin or acenocoumarol, so your doctor may need to check your INR.

Calcium, magnesium and zinc reduce the absorption of some antibiotics (tetracyclines and ciprofloxacin), thyroid medicine, iron and bisphosphonates. Take them at least 2 hours apart, or as your doctor advises.
Cholestyramine and sevelamer reduce calcitriol absorption, and corticosteroids can reduce its effect.

Not expected to affect your ability to drive.

Tell your doctor if you have severe liver disease, as the dose may need adjusting.

Do not take other vitamin D or calcium supplements unless your doctor advises it.
Keep at least 2 hours between this capsule and iron tablets, thyroid medicine, or antibiotics such as ciprofloxacin or doxycycline.
Include calcium-rich foods such as milk, curd, paneer, ragi and green leafy vegetables.
Drink plenty of water, and tell your doctor if you have had kidney stones.
See your doctor if you notice excessive thirst, frequent urination, nausea, constipation, confusion or unusual tiredness, which can be signs of high calcium.

clinical.summary: Ramnova capsule combining esomeprazole 40 mg, a proton pump inhibitor that reduces stomach acid, with domperidone 30 mg in sustained-release form, a prokinetic agent.
introduction: ESORUSK-D capsules combine esomeprazole 40 mg, which reduces stomach acid, with domperidone 30 mg in sustained-release form, which helps the stomach empty faster. uses: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GERD), including heartburn and acid regurgitation

benefits.text: In GERD, stomach acid flows back into the food pipe, causing heartburn and irritation. Esomeprazole lowers acid production, which relieves symptoms and allows the food pipe to heal. Domperidone helps food move through the stomach faster, reducing bloating, fullness and the backflow of acid. Your doctor will decide how long you need to take it; do not stop or continue it without their advice.

sideEffects: Abdominal pain, diarrhoea, constipation or wind
clinical.howToUse: Take this medicine in the dose and for the length of time your doctor advises. Swallow the capsule whole on an empty stomach, 30 to 60 minutes before a meal. Do not chew, crush or open it.
clinical.howItWorks: ESORUSK-D combines two medicines. Esomeprazole is a proton pump inhibitor that blocks the pumps in the stomach lining that produce acid. Domperidone is a prokinetic that increases the movement of the stomach and intestines, helping food pass through faster and reducing reflux, bloating and nausea. The sustained-release form releases domperidone gradually through the day.
warnings: Domperidone can affect heart rhythm (QT prolongation). The risk is higher in people over 60, at higher doses and with other medicines that affect heart rhythm. It should be used at the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible time, as decided by your doctor.
Long-term use of esomeprazole, especially beyond 3 months, may lower magnesium and vitamin B12 levels and increase the risk of bone fractures.
It may slightly increase the risk of certain gut infections.
Tell your doctor before starting if you have unexplained weight loss, difficulty swallowing, vomiting of blood or black stools.
contraindications: Heart conditions such as heart failure, or a known abnormal heart rhythm (QT prolongation)
Moderate or severe liver disease
Bleeding, blockage or perforation of the stomach or intestines
A prolactin-secreting pituitary tumour (prolactinoma)
Use with strong CYP3A4-blocking medicines such as ketoconazole, itraconazole or clarithromycin, or with the HIV medicine nelfinavir
Allergy to esomeprazole, similar acid-reducing medicines, domperidone or any other ingredient
interactions: Medicines that affect heart rhythm, such as some antiarrhythmics, antipsychotics like haloperidol, and antidepressants like citalopram or escitalopram, should not be combined with domperidone.
Esomeprazole can reduce the effect of clopidogrel, so the two should not be used together.
Esomeprazole can change the levels of warfarin, methotrexate, digoxin, phenytoin and diazepam, so your doctor may need to monitor you.
Esomeprazole reduces the absorption of some antifungals, such as ketoconazole and itraconazole, and the HIV medicine atazanavir.

safetyAdvice.note: It is not known whether alcohol is safe with this medicine. Alcohol can also worsen acid reflux, so limit it and ask your doctor.
Use only if your doctor considers that the benefits outweigh the possible risks.
Not recommended. Domperidone passes into breast milk and may affect the baby.

Avoid lying down for 2 to 3 hours after eating, and raise the head of your bed if symptoms are worse at night.
Get urgent medical help if you notice a fast or irregular heartbeat, fainting or fits.
See your doctor if you have severe or persistent watery diarrhoea, or if your symptoms do not improve.
Do not take it for longer than your doctor advises. Domperidone is used for the shortest time needed.

uses: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GERD), including heartburn and acid regurgitation
Indigestion (dyspepsia) with bloating and early fullness caused by slow stomach emptying

benefits.text: In GERD, stomach acid flows back into the food pipe, causing heartburn and irritation. Esomeprazole lowers acid production, relieving symptoms and allowing the food pipe to heal. Levosulpiride helps the stomach empty faster, so less acid is pushed back up. Your doctor will decide how long you need to take it.

When the stomach empties slowly, food stays longer and causes bloating, early fullness, nausea and discomfort. Levosulpiride improves the movement of the stomach and gut to ease these symptoms, while esomeprazole reduces acid-related pain.

sideEffects: Diarrhoea, constipation, wind or abdominal pain
Breast swelling or tenderness, milk discharge or changes to periods (caused by raised prolactin)
Rarely, tremor, stiffness or abnormal movements
clinical.howToUse: Take this medicine in the dose and for the length of time your doctor advises. Swallow the capsule whole on an empty stomach, preferably in the morning about an hour before a meal. Do not chew, crush or open it.
clinical.howItWorks: ESORUSK-LS combines two medicines. Esomeprazole is a proton pump inhibitor that blocks the pumps in the stomach lining that produce acid. Levosulpiride blocks dopamine receptors in the gut, which increases the movement of the stomach and intestines, helping food pass through and reducing reflux, bloating and nausea. The sustained-release form releases levosulpiride gradually through the day.
warnings: Levosulpiride can raise prolactin levels, which may cause breast enlargement or tenderness, milk discharge, period changes or reduced sex drive. These usually reverse when treatment stops.
Rarely it can cause tremor, stiffness or abnormal movements. It can also affect heart rhythm (QT prolongation), especially with other medicines that do the same.

Stop taking it and get urgent medical help if you develop a high fever with muscle stiffness, confusion or sweating. These can be signs of a rare but serious reaction (neuroleptic malignant syndrome).
Use with care in older people, especially those with dementia, and in people at risk of blood clots.
Long-term use of esomeprazole, especially beyond 3 months, may lower magnesium and vitamin B12 levels and increase the risk of bone fractures.
contraindications: Pregnancy and breastfeeding
Epilepsy, mania or bipolar disorder
Phaeochromocytoma (an adrenal gland tumour), because of the risk of a dangerous rise in blood pressure
Bleeding, blockage or perforation of the stomach or intestines
Breast cancer or a prolactin-secreting pituitary tumour (prolactinoma)
Use with the HIV medicine nelfinavir
Allergy to esomeprazole, similar acid-reducing medicines, levosulpiride or any other ingredient
interactions: Alcohol, sleeping tablets, strong painkillers and other medicines that cause drowsiness can increase sleepiness.
Medicines that affect heart rhythm, or that lower potassium or magnesium (such as some water tablets), should be avoided with levosulpiride.
Anticholinergic medicines and opioid painkillers can reduce levosulpiride's effect on the gut.
Esomeprazole can reduce the effect of clopidogrel, so the two should not be used together.
Esomeprazole can change the levels of warfarin, methotrexate, digoxin, phenytoin and diazepam, and reduces the absorption of ketoconazole, itraconazole and atazanavir.

safetyAdvice.note: Avoid alcohol. It increases drowsiness and can also worsen acid reflux.
Must not be used during pregnancy. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning a pregnancy.
Must not be used while breastfeeding.
Can cause drowsiness or reduced alertness. Do not drive or use machines if you are affected.
Levosulpiride is removed through the kidneys. Tell your doctor if you have kidney disease, as the dose may need adjusting.
Tell your doctor if you have severe liver disease, as the dose may need adjusting.

quickTips: Take it about an hour before breakfast.
Avoid alcohol, and limit tea, coffee, chocolate and spicy or fatty food, which can worsen reflux.
Eat smaller meals and avoid lying down for 2 to 3 hours after eating.
Do not take it for longer than your doctor advises.

See your doctor if you have severe or persistent watery diarrhoea, or if your symptoms do not improve.

name: PIPROSHOT 4.5g
sourceDescription: Piperacillin & Tazobactam Injection IP Injection
displayDescription: Piperacillin and tazobactam injection

clinical.summary: Ramnova injection combining piperacillin, a broad-spectrum penicillin antibiotic, with tazobactam, a beta-lactamase inhibitor. For use in hospital and clinical settings under medical supervision.
introduction: PIPROSHOT 4.5 g is an injectable antibiotic that combines piperacillin 4 g, a broad-spectrum penicillin, with tazobactam 500 mg, which protects piperacillin from bacterial enzymes. It is used in hospital to treat serious bacterial infections, including severe pneumonia, complicated urinary tract and abdominal infections, skin and soft tissue infections, and fever in patients with very low white blood cell counts.

It is given by a doctor or nurse as a slow infusion into a vein, usually every 6 to 8 hours. The most common side effect is diarrhoea. Tell your doctor straight away if you have ever had an allergic reaction to penicillin or any other antibiotic.
uses: Severe pneumonia, including hospital-acquired and ventilator-associated pneumonia
Complicated urinary tract infections, including kidney infection (pyelonephritis)
Complicated skin and soft tissue infections, including diabetic foot infections
Bloodstream infections linked to any of the above
Fever in patients with very low white blood cell counts (neutropenic fever) due to suspected bacterial infection

benefits.text: Piperacillin with tazobactam is active against many bacteria that cause hospital-acquired and ventilator-associated pneumonia, including Pseudomonas. Treating the infection promptly helps clear the lungs, ease breathing and reduce the risk of complications.

benefits.use: Complicated urinary tract and abdominal infections
benefits.text: Infections of the kidneys, urinary tract or abdomen are often caused by a mix of bacteria. Its broad range of activity covers many of these organisms, helping to control the infection and stop it spreading to the bloodstream.

benefits.use: Skin, soft tissue and diabetic foot infections
benefits.text: Deep skin and diabetic foot infections can involve several types of bacteria. This combination helps stop the infection spreading and supports healing alongside proper wound care.

People with very low white blood cell counts, for example during chemotherapy, can develop life-threatening infections. Starting a broad-spectrum antibiotic such as this one quickly is an important part of their care.

sideEffects: Pain, swelling or redness where the infusion is given
clinical.howToUse: This medicine is given only by a doctor or nurse in a hospital or clinic. It is dissolved and given as an infusion into a vein over about 30 minutes. Your doctor will decide the dose and how long treatment lasts, based on the infection and how well your kidneys work.
clinical.howItWorks: Piperacillin is a penicillin antibiotic that stops bacteria from building their cell walls, so they burst and die. Many bacteria make enzymes called beta-lactamases that destroy penicillins. Tazobactam blocks these enzymes, so piperacillin can work against a wider range of bacteria.
warnings: Serious, sometimes life-threatening allergic reactions, including severe skin reactions, can occur. Tell your doctor about any previous antibiotic allergy.
It can cause a serious bowel infection (Clostridioides difficile colitis). Report severe or persistent diarrhoea.
It may cause bleeding problems and low potassium levels, so your doctor may check your blood during treatment.
It contains a significant amount of sodium. Tell your doctor if you are on a low-salt diet or have heart failure.
In seriously ill patients it may slow kidney recovery, particularly with vancomycin. High doses can rarely cause fits, especially in people with kidney problems.
contraindications: Allergy to piperacillin, tazobactam or any other penicillin
A previous severe allergic reaction to any beta-lactam antibiotic, such as a cephalosporin or carbapenem
interactions: Probenecid increases the levels of piperacillin and tazobactam in the blood.
People taking blood thinners, including heparin and warfarin, may need more frequent blood clotting tests.
Piperacillin can raise methotrexate levels, which may need monitoring.
It can prolong the effect of muscle relaxants such as vecuronium used during surgery.
Using it with vancomycin increases the risk of kidney injury. Aminoglycoside antibiotics must be given separately, not mixed in the same infusion.

safetyAdvice.note: No harmful interaction is known. Avoiding alcohol can help your recovery from infection.
Used during pregnancy only when your doctor considers it clearly needed.
Small amounts pass into breast milk. Your doctor will weigh the benefits; watch your baby for diarrhoea or rash.
Its effect on driving has not been studied. Do not drive if you feel dizzy or unwell.
The dose is reduced in kidney disease, and your kidney function will be monitored, especially if you are seriously ill.
No dose change is usually needed, but tell your doctor about any liver problem.

quickTips: Before the first dose, tell your doctor or nurse about any past allergy to penicillins, cephalosporins or other antibiotics.
Tell staff immediately if you develop an itchy rash, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing during or after the infusion.
Complete the full course your doctor prescribes, even if you start to feel better.
Report diarrhoea that is severe, watery or bloody, or that continues, even weeks after treatment ends.
Report any unusual bleeding or bruising.

clinical.summary: Ramnova tablet combining tamsulosin hydrochloride 0.4 mg in sustained-release form, an alpha-blocker, with dutasteride 0.5 mg, a 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor.
introduction: PROSTEOSOL-D tablets combine tamsulosin hydrochloride 0.4 mg in sustained-release form with dutasteride 0.5 mg. It is used in men to treat the symptoms of an enlarged prostate (benign prostatic hyperplasia, BPH), such as a weak stream, difficulty starting and needing to pass urine often or urgently, and to lower the risk of urinary retention and prostate surgery.

Take one tablet a day, about 30 minutes after the same meal each day, exactly as your doctor prescribes. Tamsulosin starts working within days, but dutasteride can take several months to have its full effect. Common side effects include dizziness and changes in sexual function. It is for men only; women and children should not handle broken tablets.
uses: Moderate to severe symptoms of an enlarged prostate (benign prostatic hyperplasia, BPH)
Reducing the risk of sudden inability to pass urine (acute urinary retention) and the need for prostate surgery

benefits.text: As the prostate grows, it squeezes the urine tube, causing a weak stream, straining, dribbling and frequent trips to the toilet, including at night. Tamsulosin relaxes the muscles in the prostate and bladder neck so urine flows more easily, often within days. Dutasteride gradually shrinks the prostate, giving further improvement over 3 to 6 months.

benefits.use: Lower risk of urinary retention and surgery
benefits.text: By shrinking the prostate over time, dutasteride reduces the chance of suddenly being unable to pass urine and of needing prostate surgery. Taking it regularly, as your doctor advises, gives the most benefit.

sideEffects: Dizziness, especially when standing up quickly
Difficulty getting or keeping an erection, or reduced sex drive
Changes in ejaculation, including less semen
Rarely, a prolonged and painful erection (priapism), which needs urgent medical help
clinical.howToUse: Take one tablet a day, or as your doctor advises, about 30 minutes after the same meal each day. Swallow it whole with water; do not chew, crush or break it.
clinical.howItWorks: PROSTEOSOL-D combines two medicines that work in different ways. Tamsulosin is an alpha-blocker that relaxes the smooth muscle in the prostate and at the neck of the bladder, making it easier to pass urine. Dutasteride is a 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor that lowers dihydrotestosterone (DHT), the hormone that makes the prostate grow, so the prostate gradually shrinks.
warnings: It can cause a sudden fall in blood pressure when you stand up, leading to dizziness or fainting, especially at the start of treatment.
Dutasteride lowers PSA levels by about half, which affects prostate cancer screening. Your doctor will take this into account and may check you regularly.
Before cataract or glaucoma surgery, tell your eye surgeon, as tamsulosin can cause 'floppy iris syndrome' during the operation.
Report any breast lumps, pain or nipple discharge to your doctor.
Get urgent medical help for a painful erection that lasts more than 4 hours.
A slightly higher rate of heart failure has been seen with this combination, so tell your doctor if you have heart problems.
contraindications: Women, children and adolescents
Severe liver disease
A history of dizziness or fainting caused by low blood pressure on standing (orthostatic hypotension)
Allergy to tamsulosin, dutasteride, other 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors such as finasteride, or any other ingredient
interactions: Other alpha-blockers, such as prazosin, alfuzosin or doxazosin, must not be taken with it.
Erectile dysfunction medicines such as sildenafil or tadalafil can lower blood pressure further and cause dizziness.
Strong CYP3A4 blockers such as ketoconazole are not recommended, and CYP2D6 blockers such as paroxetine need caution, because they raise tamsulosin levels.
Tell your doctor if you take warfarin or medicines for blood pressure.

safetyAdvice.note: Alcohol can make dizziness and low blood pressure worse. Limit alcohol and ask your doctor.
For men only. Women who are or may become pregnant must not handle broken or crushed tablets, as dutasteride can harm a male baby.
Not for use by women.
Can cause dizziness or blurred vision. Do not drive or use machines if you are affected.
Tell your doctor if you have severe kidney disease.
Must not be used in severe liver disease. Tell your doctor about any liver problem.

quickTips: Take it at the same time each day, about 30 minutes after a meal.
Get up slowly from sitting or lying down, especially when you first start, to avoid dizziness or fainting.
Tell your eye surgeon that you take, or have taken, this medicine before any cataract or glaucoma surgery.
Use a condom if your partner is or may become pregnant, as dutasteride passes into semen.
Do not donate blood while taking it and for at least 6 months after stopping.
Remind your doctor that you take it before any PSA blood test, as it lowers PSA levels.

clinical.summary: Ramnova capsule combining rabeprazole 20 mg, a proton pump inhibitor that reduces stomach acid, with domperidone 30 mg in sustained-release form, a prokinetic agent.
introduction: RUSKIRAB-DSR capsules combine rabeprazole 20 mg, which reduces stomach acid, with domperidone 30 mg in sustained-release form, which helps the stomach empty faster. It is used to treat gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GERD), relieving heartburn, acid regurgitation, bloating and nausea.

Take one capsule on an empty stomach, about an hour before your first meal, exactly as your doctor prescribes. Common side effects include headache, diarrhoea and dry mouth. It must not be used during pregnancy or breastfeeding, and because domperidone can affect heart rhythm, tell your doctor about any heart problems and every other medicine you take.
uses: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GERD), including heartburn and acid regurgitation
Indigestion with bloating, fullness and nausea

benefits.text: In GERD, stomach acid flows back into the food pipe, causing heartburn and irritation. Rabeprazole lowers acid production, relieving symptoms and allowing the food pipe to heal, while domperidone helps food move through the stomach faster, reducing the backflow of acid. Your doctor will decide how long you need to take it; do not stop or continue it without their advice.
Domperidone helps the stomach empty more quickly, easing bloating, early fullness, nausea and upper abdominal discomfort, while rabeprazole reduces acid-related pain.

clinical.howToUse: Take this medicine in the dose and for the length of time your doctor advises. Swallow the capsule whole on an empty stomach, about an hour before your first meal. Do not chew, crush or open it.
clinical.howItWorks: RUSKIRAB-DSR combines two medicines. Rabeprazole is a proton pump inhibitor that blocks the pumps in the stomach lining that produce acid. Domperidone is a prokinetic that increases the movement of the stomach and intestines, helping food pass through faster and reducing reflux, bloating and nausea. The sustained-release form releases domperidone gradually through the day.
warnings: Domperidone can affect heart rhythm (QT prolongation). The risk is higher in people over 60, at higher doses and with other medicines that affect heart rhythm. It should be used at the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible time, as decided by your doctor.
Long-term use of rabeprazole, especially beyond 3 months, may lower magnesium and vitamin B12 levels and increase the risk of bone fractures.
It may slightly increase the risk of certain gut infections.
Tell your doctor before starting if you have unexplained weight loss, difficulty swallowing, vomiting of blood or black stools.
contraindications: Pregnancy and breastfeeding
Heart conditions such as heart failure, or a known abnormal heart rhythm (QT prolongation)
Moderate or severe liver disease
Bleeding, blockage or perforation of the stomach or intestines
A prolactin-secreting pituitary tumour (prolactinoma)
Use with strong CYP3A4-blocking medicines such as ketoconazole, itraconazole or clarithromycin
Allergy to rabeprazole, similar acid-reducing medicines, domperidone or any other ingredient
interactions: Medicines that affect heart rhythm, such as some antiarrhythmics, antipsychotics like haloperidol, and antidepressants like citalopram or escitalopram, should not be combined with domperidone.
Rabeprazole sharply reduces the absorption of ketoconazole and itraconazole, and should not be used with the HIV medicine atazanavir.
Rabeprazole can raise high-dose methotrexate levels, which may need monitoring.

safetyAdvice.note: Alcohol can increase drowsiness and worsen acid reflux. Limit it and ask your doctor.
Must not be used during pregnancy.
Must not be used while breastfeeding.
May cause dizziness or drowsiness. Do not drive until you know how it affects you.
Your doctor may need to adjust the dose or review treatment if you have severe kidney disease.
Not recommended in moderate or severe liver disease. Tell your doctor if you have any liver problem.

quickTips: Take it about an hour before your first meal, at the same time each day.
Eat smaller, more frequent meals, avoid spicy or oily food, and do not lie down straight after eating.
See your doctor if your symptoms have not improved after 2 weeks.
Get urgent medical help if you notice a fast or irregular heartbeat, fainting or fits.
See your doctor if you have severe or persistent watery diarrhoea or fever.
Do not take it for longer than your doctor advises. Domperidone is used for the shortest time needed.

clinical.summary: Ramnova ursodeoxycholic acid 300 mg uncoated tablets. Ursodeoxycholic acid is a bile acid used in the management of certain liver and gallbladder conditions.
introduction: URSORAM 300 tablets contain 300 mg of ursodeoxycholic acid, a bile acid. It is used to dissolve cholesterol gallstones and to treat certain long-term liver conditions, including primary biliary cholangitis. It works by improving the flow of bile and lowering the cholesterol in it, which helps gallstones dissolve and protects liver cells.

Take URSORAM after a meal with water or milk, exactly as your doctor prescribes. Treatment usually lasts several months or longer, so keep taking it even if you feel better. The most common side effect is diarrhoea or loose stools. Tell your doctor about any other medicines you take, and if you are pregnant or breastfeeding.
uses: Dissolving cholesterol gallstones in people whose gallbladder is still working
Liver disease associated with cystic fibrosis

benefits.text: Ursodeoxycholic acid lowers the amount of cholesterol in bile, which allows small cholesterol stones in a working gallbladder to dissolve slowly. This can take several months, so take it regularly for as long as your doctor advises. Your doctor may arrange scans to check progress.

In PBC, the small bile ducts inside the liver are gradually damaged and bile builds up. Ursodeoxycholic acid improves bile flow and protects liver cells from harmful bile acids, which can slow the disease and improve liver test results. It is usually taken long term.

benefits.use: Liver disease associated with cystic fibrosis
benefits.text: In cystic fibrosis, thick bile can block the small bile ducts and damage the liver. Ursodeoxycholic acid helps bile flow more easily and protects liver cells. In the UK it is approved for this use in children aged 6 to 18.

sideEffects: Diarrhoea or loose stools (the most common side effect)
clinical.howToUse: Take this medicine in the dose and for the length of time your doctor advises. Swallow the tablet whole with water or milk; do not chew or crush it. Take it with or after food.
clinical.howItWorks: URSORAM contains ursodeoxycholic acid, a bile acid that occurs naturally in small amounts in the body. It reduces the cholesterol the liver releases into bile, which helps cholesterol gallstones dissolve. It also replaces more harmful bile acids, improves bile flow and protects liver cells from damage.

Limit alcohol during treatment

Blockage of the bile ducts

Calcified gallstones, or a gallbladder that does not contract properly
An active stomach or duodenal ulcer
In children with biliary atresia: an unsuccessful operation to restore bile flow
Allergy to ursodeoxycholic acid or any other ingredient of the tablet
interactions: Antacids containing aluminium or magnesium (such as magaldrate), cholestyramine and colestipol can reduce absorption. Take ursodeoxycholic acid at least 2 hours apart from them.
Medicines containing oestrogen, including hormonal contraceptives, can raise cholesterol in bile and may reduce its effect on gallstones.

Not recommended unless clearly necessary. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor.
Only very small amounts are expected to pass into breast milk. Ask your doctor before use.
Not expected to affect your ability to drive.

Used to treat certain liver conditions. Take only as prescribed, with regular liver tests.

Avoid high-fat, oily meals and limit alcohol.

Your doctor will check your liver tests regularly, especially in the first few months.
Get medical help quickly for worsening jaundice, severe itching, dark urine or ongoing abdominal pain.
Don't stop taking it without speaking to your doctor.

It is active against many bacteria that cause pneumonia and infections inside the abdomen. Tazobactam blocks the enzymes some bacteria use to resist ceftriaxone, helping it work against a wider range of bacteria.
It treats complicated urinary tract and kidney infections, as well as infections of bones and joints, which may need several days or weeks of treatment as decided by your doctor.

introduction: KRUJOKAST-B tablets combine bilastine 20 mg, a non-drowsy antihistamine, with montelukast 10 mg, a leukotriene receptor antagonist. It is used to relieve allergic rhinitis and hay fever (sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itchy and watery eyes) and hives, and to help control asthma, particularly when allergies and asthma occur together.

Take one tablet once a day on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after food or fruit juice, exactly as your doctor prescribes. It is for adults and adolescents aged 15 and over. Montelukast can occasionally cause mood or behaviour changes, so tell your doctor straight away if you notice any.

benefits.text: During an allergic reaction the body releases histamine and leukotrienes, which cause sneezing, a runny or blocked nose and itchy, watery eyes. Bilastine blocks histamine to relieve sneezing, itching and a runny nose, while montelukast blocks leukotrienes, which can help with nasal congestion, especially in people who also have asthma.

Leukotrienes narrow and inflame the airways. Montelukast blocks them, helping to prevent asthma symptoms, including those triggered by exercise or allergies. It is a preventer and does not relieve a sudden attack.
Bilastine reduces the itching and raised red wheals of hives by blocking histamine, the main chemical behind them.

sideEffects: Rarely, mood changes, disturbed sleep or vivid dreams
clinical.howToUse: Take one tablet once a day, or as your doctor advises, at the same time each day. Take it on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after eating or drinking fruit juice, as food reduces how much bilastine is absorbed. Swallow it whole with water.
clinical.howItWorks: During an allergic reaction, the body releases chemicals including histamine and leukotrienes. Bilastine is a long-acting antihistamine that blocks histamine H1 receptors, relieving sneezing, itching and hives without usually causing drowsiness. Montelukast blocks leukotriene receptors in the airways and nose, reducing swelling, mucus and narrowing of the airways.
warnings: Montelukast can cause mood and behaviour changes, such as agitation, sleep problems, depression and suicidal thoughts, in people of all ages. Stop taking it and contact your doctor if these occur.
It does not relieve a sudden asthma attack, and it must not replace inhaled or oral steroid treatment unless your doctor advises.
Rarely, people taking montelukast have developed inflammation of the blood vessels, with rash, tingling, worsening breathing or sinus pain. Tell your doctor if you notice these.
Bilastine should be used with caution in people with heart rhythm problems or low potassium or magnesium.
It is not suitable for children under 15 years.
contraindications: Allergy to bilastine, montelukast or any other ingredient
interactions: Food and grapefruit or other fruit juices reduce the absorption of bilastine.
Ketoconazole, erythromycin, ciclosporin, ritonavir and diltiazem increase bilastine levels; avoid them if you also have moderate or severe kidney disease.
Phenobarbital, phenytoin and rifampicin can reduce the effect of montelukast.
Gemfibrozil increases montelukast levels.
Use caution with other medicines that affect heart rhythm.

introduction: OPTIBREATHE-N tablets combine acebrophylline 100 mg, which relaxes the airways and helps clear mucus, with acetylcysteine 600 mg, which thins thick phlegm so it is easier to cough up. It is used in asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), including chronic bronchitis, to ease breathlessness, chest tightness and cough with sticky mucus.

Take it exactly as your doctor prescribes, usually after food. Common side effects include nausea, stomach upset and headache. It does not relieve a sudden asthma attack, so keep your reliever inhaler with you, and tell your doctor if you have heart, liver, kidney or thyroid problems or a stomach ulcer.

benefits.text: In asthma the airways tighten and fill with sticky mucus. Acebrophylline relaxes the airway muscles and improves mucus clearance, while acetylcysteine thins the mucus, helping you breathe and cough more easily. It is used alongside your inhalers, not instead of them.

In COPD and chronic bronchitis, narrowed airways and thick phlegm cause breathlessness and a persistent cough. By opening the airways and loosening phlegm, this combination can make daily activities easier and coughing more productive.

sideEffects: Rarely, a fast heartbeat or chest tightness
clinical.howToUse: Take this medicine in the dose and for the length of time your doctor advises, preferably after food to reduce stomach upset. Swallow the tablet whole with water; do not chew or crush it. Drink plenty of fluids during the day to help loosen mucus.
clinical.howItWorks: Acebrophylline combines ambroxol, which helps the lungs produce thinner mucus and clear it more easily, with a theophylline-like compound that relaxes the muscles of the airways. Acetylcysteine breaks the chemical bonds that make mucus thick and sticky, so phlegm becomes thinner and easier to cough up.
warnings: Acetylcysteine can occasionally cause tightening of the airways, especially in people with asthma. Stop taking it and seek help if this happens.
Use with caution in older people and in people with heart disease, high blood pressure, heart failure, an overactive thyroid, very low blood oxygen levels or a history of stomach ulcers.
Rarely, serious skin reactions have been reported with both ingredients. Stop taking it and seek medical help if a widespread rash, blistering or peeling develops.

contraindications: Allergy to acebrophylline, ambroxol, theophylline or similar medicines (xanthines), acetylcysteine or any other ingredient
A recent heart attack

Severe liver or kidney disease
Breastfeeding
interactions: Cough suppressants should not be taken with it, as they stop you from clearing the loosened mucus.
Take oral antibiotics at least 2 hours apart, as acetylcysteine may reduce their effect.
It may increase the effect of nitroglycerin (glyceryl trinitrate), which can cause headache or low blood pressure.
Activated charcoal reduces the effect of acetylcysteine.
Acebrophylline is related to theophylline, so tell your doctor if you take theophylline or other medicines for breathing.

clinical.summary: Ramnova rifaximin 200 mg film-coated tablets. Rifaximin is an antibacterial that acts mainly within the gut because very little of it is absorbed into the bloodstream.
introduction: RAMOMIN-200 tablets contain rifaximin 200 mg, an antibiotic that acts mainly inside the gut because very little is absorbed into the bloodstream. It is used to treat infectious diarrhoea and other intestinal infections, to help lower ammonia in liver disease, and to reduce gut bacteria around bowel surgery.

Take it with or without food, exactly as your doctor prescribes. For diarrhoea it is usually taken for only a few days. Common side effects include nausea, bloating and headache, and it may turn your urine reddish, which is harmless.
uses: Acute and chronic intestinal infections caused by non-invasive bacteria
Pre- and post-operative prophylaxis in gastrointestinal surgery

benefits.text: Rifaximin acts against a wide range of gut bacteria in intestinal infections caused by bacteria that do not invade the gut wall. Because it stays in the gut, it works where the infection is.

Rifaximin kills many of the bacteria that cause traveller's and other infectious diarrhoea, such as non-invasive strains of E. coli, and can shorten the illness. It is not suitable for diarrhoea with fever or blood in the stool, which needs other treatment.

In advanced liver disease, gut bacteria produce ammonia, which can build up and affect the brain (hepatic encephalopathy), causing confusion and drowsiness. Rifaximin reduces these bacteria, lowering ammonia and helping to prevent episodes, usually alongside lactulose.
It may be used to reduce the number of gut bacteria before and after bowel surgery, lowering the risk of infection.

sideEffects: Swelling of the ankles or legs, mainly in people with liver disease
Reddish discoloration of the urine, which is harmless
clinical.howToUse: Take this medicine in the dose and for the length of time your doctor advises. Swallow the tablet whole with water, with or without food. For infectious diarrhoea, treatment usually lasts no more than 3 days; for liver-related conditions it may be longer.
clinical.howItWorks: Rifaximin is an antibiotic related to rifampicin. It blocks a bacterial enzyme needed to make RNA, so bacteria cannot produce the proteins they need to grow. Less than 1% is absorbed, so it stays in the gut, where it acts on the bacteria that cause diarrhoea and on those that produce ammonia.
warnings: It is not suitable for diarrhoea with fever or blood in the stool, which may be caused by bacteria that invade the gut wall.
Like other antibiotics, it can cause a serious bowel infection (Clostridioides difficile). See your doctor if diarrhoea becomes severe or persistent.
Rarely, serious skin reactions have been reported, especially in people with liver disease. Stop taking it and seek help if a widespread rash or blistering develops.
Use with caution in severe liver disease.
contraindications: Allergy to rifaximin or other rifamycin antibiotics, such as rifampicin or rifabutin
Blockage of the intestines
interactions: Ciclosporin can greatly increase the amount of rifaximin absorbed.
It can change the effect of warfarin, with both higher and lower INR reported, so your INR should be checked closely.
In people with liver disease it may reduce the effect of hormonal contraceptives, so ask your doctor whether extra contraception is needed.

safetyAdvice.note: Avoid alcohol. It irritates the gut and is harmful in liver disease.
Not recommended during pregnancy unless your doctor considers it essential.
It is not known whether rifaximin passes into breast milk. Ask your doctor before use.
Not expected to affect driving, although dizziness can occasionally occur.
There is limited information in kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have kidney problems.
Use with caution in severe liver disease. Your doctor will monitor you.

quickTips: Drink plenty of fluids, or oral rehydration solution (ORS), while you have diarrhoea.
Don't worry if your urine turns reddish; this is harmless.
See your doctor if diarrhoea does not improve within 2 to 3 days, or if you develop fever or blood in your stool.
Complete the course your doctor prescribes.
If you take warfarin, your INR may need checking more often.
If you have liver disease, keep taking your other treatments, such as lactulose, as prescribed.

clinical.summary: Ramnova cefpodoxime dry syrup for children, 100 mg per 5 ml, supplied as 15 g of powder that is reconstituted to make 30 mL of oral suspension. Cefpodoxime is a third-generation cephalosporin antibiotic.
introduction: SIZEPOD-100 is a dry syrup for children containing cefpodoxime 100 mg per 5 ml (as cefpodoxime proxetil), a third-generation cephalosporin antibiotic. The powder is mixed with water to make 30 ml of oral suspension. It is used to treat bacterial infections of the ear, throat, tonsils, sinuses and chest.

Give it exactly as your child's doctor prescribes, usually twice a day, and finish the full course even if your child feels better. The most common side effects are diarrhoea, nappy rash and vomiting. Tell the doctor if your child has ever had an allergic reaction to penicillin or any other antibiotic.

benefits.text: Middle ear infections are common in young children and cause ear pain, fever and irritability. Cefpodoxime kills the bacteria most often responsible, easing pain and fever, usually within a few days.

Bacterial sore throats and tonsillitis cause pain, fever and difficulty swallowing. Treating them with an antibiotic relieves symptoms and helps prevent complications. Completing the full course is important.
Cefpodoxime is active against many bacteria that cause sinus infections and pneumonia. It helps clear the infection, reducing cough, fever and congestion.

clinical.howToUse: Shake the bottle to loosen the powder, then add the sterile water supplied in the pack up to the ring mark on the bottle and shake well. Shake well again before each dose, and measure it with the cup or syringe provided rather than a kitchen spoon. It can be given with or without food, though giving it with food may reduce stomach upset. Keep the mixed suspension in a refrigerator, use it within 4 days, and throw away any medicine left after that.
clinical.howItWorks: Cefpodoxime is a cephalosporin antibiotic. Taken by mouth, it is absorbed and converted into its active form, which stops bacteria from building their protective cell walls, so they die. It works against bacteria, not viruses, so it will not help colds or flu.
warnings: Tell the doctor if your child has ever had an allergic reaction to penicillin. Some people allergic to penicillin also react to cephalosporins, so after a severe reaction the doctor may choose a different antibiotic.
Antibiotics can cause a serious bowel infection (Clostridioides difficile), which can appear up to two months after treatment. See a doctor for severe or persistent diarrhoea.
In children with kidney problems the dose must be adjusted, as the medicine can build up.
Using antibiotics when they are not needed, or stopping early, encourages resistant bacteria.
contraindications: Allergy to cefpodoxime or any other cephalosporin antibiotic
interactions: Antacids and acid-reducing medicines such as ranitidine or famotidine reduce absorption. Give them at least 2 hours apart.
Probenecid increases cefpodoxime levels in the blood.
Medicines that can harm the kidneys need closer monitoring when taken with it.

safetyAdvice.note: The dose needs to be reduced in kidney disease. Tell the doctor about any kidney problem.
No dose change is usually needed in liver disease.

quickTips: Finish the whole course, even if your child feels better, to stop the infection coming back.
Use only the sterile water supplied in the pack to mix the medicine.
Keep the mixed suspension in the fridge and throw it away after 4 days.
Use the measuring cup or syringe provided for accurate doses.
Give plenty of fluids if your child has diarrhoea, and see the doctor if it is severe, watery or bloody.
Stop the medicine and get urgent help if your child develops a rash, swelling of the face or lips, or difficulty breathing.
Do not keep leftover medicine for later or give it to another child.

clinical.summary: Ramnova flavoxate hydrochloride 200 mg tablets. Flavoxate is a urinary antispasmodic that helps relieve bladder spasm and related urinary symptoms.
introduction: FLAVOLEAD tablets contain flavoxate hydrochloride 200 mg, a urinary antispasmodic. It relaxes the muscles of the bladder and urinary tract to relieve painful urination, urgency, frequent urination, night-time urination and leakage, including symptoms linked to cystitis, prostatitis and urethritis.

Take it after meals, usually three times a day, exactly as your doctor prescribes. The most common side effect is nausea; it can also cause drowsiness or blurred vision. It is not recommended for children under 12, and it must not be used by people with glaucoma or difficulty passing urine.
uses: Urinary symptoms in cystitis, prostatitis, urethritis and urethrotrigonitis

benefits.text: In an overactive bladder, the bladder muscle squeezes suddenly and often, causing urgent and frequent trips to the toilet. Flavoxate relaxes this muscle, so the bladder can hold more urine and the urge becomes easier to control.

Irritation of the bladder or urethra can cause burning, pain and a constant urge to pass urine. By easing spasm in the urinary tract, flavoxate relieves these symptoms while the underlying cause is treated.

benefits.use: Night-time urination, lower abdominal pain and leakage
benefits.text: Relaxing the bladder muscle can reduce how often you wake at night to pass urine, ease discomfort above the pubic bone, and lessen leakage caused by bladder spasm.

benefits.use: Symptoms of urinary infections and inflammation
benefits.text: In cystitis, prostatitis and urethritis, flavoxate eases the painful spasm and urgency. It does not treat infection itself, so your doctor may prescribe an antibiotic alongside it.

sideEffects: Rarely, allergic reactions, a fast heartbeat or difficulty passing urine
clinical.howToUse: Take this medicine in the dose and for the length of time your doctor advises, usually one tablet three times a day. Swallow the tablet whole with water after a meal; do not chew or crush it.
clinical.howItWorks: Flavoxate is a urinary antispasmodic. It acts directly on the smooth muscle of the bladder and urinary tract, relaxing it and reducing involuntary contractions. This increases the amount of urine the bladder can hold and eases pain, urgency and frequency.
warnings: It is not recommended for children under 12 years.
Use with caution in kidney disease.
It can cause drowsiness or blurred vision. Avoid driving or operating machinery if affected.
contraindications: Glaucoma
Difficulty passing urine (urinary retention)
Blockage of the stomach or intestines, or bowel paralysis (ileus)
Bleeding in the stomach or intestines
Achalasia (a swallowing disorder of the food pipe)
Myasthenia gravis
Allergy to flavoxate or any other ingredient
interactions: No formal interaction studies have been done. Tell your doctor about all the medicines you take.
Taking it with other medicines that have anticholinergic effects, such as trihexyphenidyl, procyclidine or clozapine, may increase dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision or difficulty passing urine.

safetyAdvice.note: Alcohol can irritate the bladder and add to drowsiness. Limit it and ask your doctor.
Best avoided during pregnancy unless your doctor considers it necessary.
Should not be used while breastfeeding.
Can cause drowsiness or blurred vision. Do not drive or use machines if you are affected.
Flavoxate is mainly removed through the kidneys. Tell your doctor if you have kidney disease.
Tell your doctor if you have liver disease.

quickTips: Take it after meals to reduce nausea.
Cut down on tea, coffee, fizzy drinks and alcohol, which can irritate the bladder.
Drink enough water through the day, but reduce fluids in the evening if night-time urination is a problem.
For a dry mouth, sip water or chew sugar-free gum.
Tell your doctor if you have glaucoma or eye pain, or if you find it hard to pass urine.
See your doctor if you have fever, blood in the urine or pain in your back or side, which may mean an infection needing other treatment.

clinical.summary: Ramnova liver support suspension combining silymarin with L-ornithine L-aspartate, tricholine citrate and B-complex vitamins.
introduction: SILIRAM-MAX is a liver support nutritional suspension. Each 5 ml contains silymarin 35 mg (from milk thistle), L-ornithine L-aspartate 150 mg and tricholine citrate 275 mg, with vitamins B1, B2, B3, B5, B6 and B12. It is used as supportive care in liver conditions such as fatty liver, alongside the treatment your doctor recommends.

Shake the bottle well and take the dose your doctor or dietician advises with the measuring cup, at the same times each day. It is usually well tolerated, though mild stomach upset or diarrhoea can occur. It supports, but does not replace, treatment of the cause of liver disease, so avoid alcohol and follow your doctor's advice.
uses: Supportive care in liver disease, including fatty liver
Vitamin B-complex support in people with liver conditions

benefits.text: Silymarin is an antioxidant from milk thistle that has been studied for protecting liver cells, although results in liver disease have been mixed. L-ornithine L-aspartate supplies amino acids the liver uses to clear ammonia, a waste product that can build up when the liver is not working well. Tricholine citrate supplies choline, which the liver needs to process fat. Your doctor can advise whether it is suitable alongside your other treatment.

Liver disease often reduces appetite and the body's stores of B vitamins. Each 5 ml provides the daily recommended amount of vitamins B1, B2, B3, B5, B6 and B12, which the body needs to turn food into energy and keep nerves healthy.

clinical.howToUse: Shake the bottle well before use. Take the dose your doctor or dietician advises using the measuring cup provided, at the same times each day. Keep the cap tightly closed and store below 25°C, away from light and moisture.
clinical.howItWorks: Silymarin, taken from milk thistle seeds, is an antioxidant that is thought to help protect liver cells from toxins. L-ornithine L-aspartate provides two amino acids that the liver uses to convert ammonia into urea, which the body then removes. Tricholine citrate supplies choline, which the liver uses to move fat out of its cells. The B vitamins help replace nutrients that are often low in liver disease.
warnings: This suspension supports, but does not replace, treatment of the underlying cause of liver disease.
People allergic to plants in the daisy family, such as ragweed, chrysanthemum or marigold, may react to silymarin.
Avoid taking other vitamin B supplements at the same time unless your doctor advises it.
It contains sugar, so people with diabetes should check with their doctor before use.
It contains the colour tartrazine, which can cause allergic reactions in some people, particularly those sensitive to aspirin.
It contains polyols, which can have a laxative effect.
contraindications: Severe kidney disease
Allergy to milk thistle, plants in the daisy family, or any other ingredient
interactions: Silymarin may lower blood sugar slightly, so people taking diabetes medicines should monitor their sugar levels.
Information on interactions with this combination is limited, so tell your doctor about all the medicines and supplements you take.

safetyAdvice.note: Avoid alcohol completely. It damages the liver and works against this treatment.
Safety in pregnancy has not been established. Use only if your doctor advises it.
There is not enough information on use while breastfeeding. Ask your doctor first.
Not known to affect driving, but liver disease itself can cause drowsiness or confusion. Do not drive if you are affected.
Not suitable for people with severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor about any kidney problem.
Intended for liver conditions. Use only under your doctor's supervision, with regular liver tests.

quickTips: Shake the bottle well and use the measuring cup for each dose.
Avoid alcohol and smoking while you take it.
Eat a balanced diet low in fried and fatty food, and stay active to help reduce liver fat.
Keep your follow-up appointments. Your doctor may check your liver and kidney tests regularly.
Tell your doctor about any other herbal products, vitamins or supplements you take.
See your doctor if you notice yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, confusion or swelling of the abdomen.

clinical.summary: Ramnova film-coated tablet combining gabapentin 100 mg with nortriptyline 10 mg for long-term nerve (neuropathic) pain.
introduction: GABASRAM NT 100 tablets combine gabapentin 100 mg with nortriptyline 10 mg. Both medicines calm overactive nerve signals, and together they are used to treat long-term nerve pain (neuropathic pain), such as pain from diabetic nerve damage, shingles or spinal problems, which often causes burning, tingling, shooting pain or numbness.

Take it as your doctor prescribes, usually once a day at bedtime, because it can make you drowsy. It may take a few weeks to work fully. Do not stop it suddenly, avoid alcohol, and tell your doctor straight away about any low mood or thoughts of self-harm.

benefits.text: Damaged nerves can send pain signals even without injury, causing burning, shooting or stabbing pain, tingling and numbness. Gabapentin, which is licensed for nerve pain, reduces these overactive signals. Low-dose nortriptyline is widely used by doctors for nerve pain because it strengthens the body's own pain-blocking pathways. Together they can relieve pain and improve sleep.
Long-term high blood sugar can damage the nerves in the feet and legs. This combination eases the burning and tingling, alongside good blood sugar control and foot care.
Pain can continue for months after a shingles rash has healed. Gabapentin is used to reduce this lingering nerve pain, and low-dose nortriptyline is often added by doctors.

sideEffects: Weight gain or swelling of the ankles
clinical.howToUse: Take this medicine in the dose and for the length of time your doctor advises, usually once a day at bedtime. Swallow the tablet whole with water, with or without food. Do not stop taking it suddenly; your doctor will reduce the dose gradually when it is time to stop.
clinical.howItWorks: Gabapentin attaches to calcium channels on nerve cells and reduces the release of chemicals that carry pain signals, calming overactive nerves. Nortriptyline is a tricyclic medicine that increases noradrenaline and serotonin levels in the spinal cord, strengthening the nervous system's natural pain-blocking pathways. At this low dose it is used for pain rather than depression, although in the UK it is licensed only for depression.
warnings: Both medicines have been linked with suicidal thoughts. Family members or carers should also watch for changes in mood or behaviour.
Gabapentin can cause serious breathing problems when taken with opioid painkillers, sleeping tablets or other sedatives, especially in older people or those with lung disease.
Gabapentin can be misused and cause dependence, especially in people with a history of substance misuse.
Nortriptyline can affect heart rhythm. Tell your doctor if you have heart disease, and get urgent help for chest pain, a racing or irregular heartbeat, or fainting.
Use with caution in epilepsy, glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, an enlarged prostate, an overactive thyroid or diabetes.
Rarely, serious allergic or skin reactions can occur. Stop taking it and seek help for a widespread rash, fever, swollen glands or swelling of the face.
It is not for use in people under 18 years.
contraindications: A recent heart attack, heart block, an irregular heart rhythm or reduced blood supply to the heart
Taking, or having taken within the last 14 days, a monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI) antidepressant
Allergy to gabapentin, nortriptyline or any other ingredient
interactions: Opioid painkillers, sleeping tablets, anti-anxiety medicines and alcohol increase drowsiness and the risk of slowed breathing.
Antacids containing aluminium or magnesium reduce gabapentin absorption; take gabapentin at least 2 hours after them.
Other antidepressants such as SSRIs, and tramadol, can cause serotonin syndrome (agitation, fever, sweating, shaking).
Fluoxetine, paroxetine, bupropion, cimetidine, diltiazem and verapamil can raise nortriptyline levels.
Medicines that affect heart rhythm, adrenaline-type decongestants and anticholinergic medicines should be used with caution.

safetyAdvice.note: Avoid alcohol. It can cause severe drowsiness and, with gabapentin, slowed breathing.
Use only if your doctor considers that the benefits outweigh the risks. Babies may have withdrawal symptoms after birth.
Small amounts pass into breast milk. Ask your doctor; your baby may need to be watched for drowsiness.
It commonly causes drowsiness, dizziness and blurred vision. Do not drive or use machines until you know how it affects you.
Gabapentin is removed by the kidneys, so the dose must be reduced in kidney disease.
Tell your doctor if you have liver disease, as nortriptyline may need a lower dose.

quickTips: Take it at bedtime to reduce daytime drowsiness.
It can take 2 to 3 weeks or longer to feel the full effect, so keep taking it as prescribed.
Do not stop suddenly, as this can cause withdrawal symptoms such as anxiety, poor sleep, nausea and sweating.
Take antacids at least 2 hours before this tablet.
Avoid alcohol and other medicines that make you sleepy unless your doctor agrees.
Use sunscreen and avoid strong sunlight, as nortriptyline can make your skin more sensitive.
Tell your doctor straight away about any low mood, unusual behaviour or thoughts of self-harm.
